provenance.author: Project assistant
provenance.scope: Targeted authored challenge, references frozen before scoring this run. Author has inspected the implementation; not blind or independent human annotation.
provenance.link_definition: A single predicted link is accepted if it addresses one of the explicitly allowed previous turns. Empty links mean abstention is expected.
provenance.role_definition: Primary communicative function in the current dialogue. Off-topic and metalinguistic non-arguments are unclassified. Rhetorical/underspecified cases should be reviewed, not treated as universal gold.
provenance.evidence_note: Any numeric or study-like examples in these fixtures are hypothetical test content, not factual claims.

cases.topic: Should schools subsidize required student uniforms?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Schools should subsidize uniforms for low income families.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I disagree because a uniform subsidy would divert money from teaching.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What evidence supports the claim about the teaching budget?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For example, a fixed school budget would have to cover both uniforms and classroom supplies.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I agree that the school budget needs protection.

cases.topic: Should public transport be free for city residents?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: City buses should be free for residents.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Removing fares would leave a funding gap for bus maintenance.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Because congestion charges could replace fare revenue, bus maintenance could still be funded.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: How would that revenue be collected?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The city would collect the charge when drivers enter the central traffic zone.

cases.topic: Should university assignments allow generative AI assistance?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Students should be allowed to use AI for brainstorming.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I do not agree that AI brainstorming helps students learn.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For instance, comparing AI suggestions can help students critique weak ideas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That example does not establish that students develop their own ideas.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What evidence would convince you that AI can support independent thinking?

cases.topic: Should universities replace lectures with online recordings?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Recorded lectures improve university attendance.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: There is no evidence that recorded lectures improve attendance.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Where is the evidence for that conclusion?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I do not have attendance data to support that conclusion.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then we should compare attendance before replacing classroom lectures.

cases.topic: Should the university library stay open overnight?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The university library should stay open overnight during exams.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: How much would overnight staffing cost?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How many students would use the library after midnight?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The overnight staffing cost would depend on the number of paid security shifts.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We do not yet know how many students would visit after midnight.

cases.topic: Should apartment buildings require recycling?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Apartment residents should separate recyclable materials.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The question "Should apartment residents separate recyclable materials?" is the title of our presentation.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Because mixed waste contaminates paper, separate bins can protect recyclable materials.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I agree that contamination makes recycling harder.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Could the building provide separate recycling bins?

cases.topic: Should the country build new nuclear power plants?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: New nuclear plants could provide steady electricity.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: However, construction delays could make new nuclear capacity arrive too late.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For example, electricity shortages may occur while a nuclear plant is still being built.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is why we should compare construction schedules with expected electricity demand.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Can you provide a source for the expected construction time?

cases.topic: Should schools provide free lunches to all students?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Schools should provide free lunches for every student.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I disagree because universal free lunches would increase the school food budget.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What is your source for the expected budget increase?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I would rather discuss the lunch menu than answer that question.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For example, a vegetarian lunch menu could reduce ingredient costs.

cases.topic: Should the city build more protected bicycle lanes?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Protected bicycle lanes would make cycling safer.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Removing car parking to build bicycle lanes would harm nearby shops.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For example, a physical barrier prevents cars from entering the bicycle lane.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: What evidence shows that bicycle barriers reduce collisions?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: According to the hypothetical road audit in this exercise, barriers reduce car entry into the cycling lane.

cases.topic: Should students be allowed to use phones in class?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Students should be allowed to use phones to look up unfamiliar terms.

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: For example, phone notifications could distract students during an exam.

cases.topic: Should public museums offer free admission?

cases.topic: Should organizations adopt a four day working week?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A four day workweek could improve employee recovery time.

turns.speaker: B

cases.topic: Should cafeterias charge diners for wasted food?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Charging diners for wasted food could reduce cafeteria waste.

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: A
